rows.requirement: Client transport: authenticated-first, then automatic guest retry on 401/403 (saved repair method f413ffa); no auth wording shown
rows.gap: Nothing blocking. Minor: a transient GoTrue/network failure in supabase.auth.getUser() also returns 401 (chat.ts:331-338), so a valid user is silently downgraded to the guest path (no tools, no live data) with no notice.

rows.requirement: Real incremental streaming (token or sentence) so the first visible text arrives before the whole generation finishes
rows.gap: Time to first byte equals the total turn time. Users see only 'سَدِيد يفكّر…' for the whole turn. Voice cannot start until the full answer exists. The owner-approved sentence streaming is not built.
rows.correction: Step 1 (keeps the safe-output gateway, small change): return createUIMessageStreamResponse right away and move the context/model work inside an async execute(). Write a 'start' chunk plus transient data-status parts ('يجمع السياق…', 'يحلّل…') so headers and bytes flow at once. The final text still goes through finalizeSadeedOutput as a single delta. Step 2 (owner flag, e.g. SADEED_SENTENCE_STREAM): streamText, then per-sentence pre-checks, with a final whole-text gateway pass that can replace what was shown. Any change here needs the four 2026-10-11 controls.

rows.requirement: Cancel/stop: user stop aborts client and server work and does not leave side effects running
rows.gap: Stop is cosmetic for the server if request.signal does not propagate. Tool writes already done in earlier steps are not undone. Stopped turns are still persisted as answers.
rows.correction: Pass request.signal into embedText/httpFetch and into supabase builders (.abortSignal()). Check request.signal.aborted between stages and skip persistence when aborted. Confirm the Workers compatibility flag for request.signal.

rows.requirement: Automatic retry (layer 2, client half): 2 backed-off retries for transient failures only, without duplicating work
rows.gap: Retries hit non-retryable statuses (wasting the shared guest bucket) while real provider failures get no retry. The user-facing promise of an automatic reconnect is false.
rows.correction: Retry only on network errors, 408 and 5xx (except ai_disabled), never on 4xx or 429. For provider errors, emit messageMetadata {retryable:true, errorCode} and let the client auto-retry on that. Do not persist provider-error lines as answers.

rows.requirement: Idempotency of side-effecting tool calls across retry/regenerate
rows.gap: Duplicate incidents, work orders, tasks or emails/SMS after a retry or 'إعادة توليد الرد'. This is a data-integrity risk.
rows.correction: The client generates one turn id per user message, sends it as x-aria-request-id and reuses it on regenerate and auto-retry. Writer tools record (user_id, turn_id, tool) and return the prior result on a repeat. Alternatively, hide 'regenerate' when the last turn executed a writer.
rows.verifier: **Verified** (adversarial pass): Confirmed: 31 tool() entries in sadeed-tools.server.ts. Writers insert without dedupe: create_task at 134-150, sec_create_incident genRef at 599-619. The outbound idempotency_key is derived from a fresh crypto.randomUUID() on every call (outbound-messaging.server.ts:441,452), so a repeat call means a repeat send. x-aria-request-id is read only at -chat-guard.ts:41 and is never set by sadeed-service.ts. The main vector is the manual regenerate button (SadeedCopilot.tsx:2186-2195). Auto-retry (1874-1885) fires only on transport/HTTP errors, because model errors come back as a 200 with mapped text, so it can duplicate only after a mid-turn disconnect.

rows.requirement: Connection interruption: a dropped connection degrades gracefully and resumes or retries once
rows.gap: Long idle connections may be cut by intermediaries (not measured). Each recovery re-pays the full cost and repeats side effects.
rows.correction: Covered by CHAT-02 step 1 (early headers plus periodic data-heartbeat parts) and CHAT-05 (idempotency). Resumable streams can come later if needed.

rows.correction: Client: one pure mapper, toArabicChatError(raw, status). It prefers message_ar, maps known codes/statuses to Arabic lines, and falls back to CONNECTION_ERROR_AR for anything without Arabic script. Server: Arabic text in chatJsonError for user-facing statuses, with the English code kept in a separate 'code' field.

rows.requirement: Provider routing, fallback and cooldown (layer 2, server half: 'تبريد المزوّد الفاشل ... المحاولة التالية تذهب لمزوّد آخر مهيأ')
rows.gap: The layer CLAUDE.md lists as preserved does not exist. A Gemini model outage or quota exhaustion means every model turn returns the mapped error line, with no alternate model and no cooldown.

rows.requirement: Guaranteed reply / no 503 to the user (layer 1)
rows.gap: A DB/RPC outage makes every chat a 503, including no-model answers (scope guard, fast recall, instant data) that cost nothing.
rows.correction: When rate or quota checks are unavailable, still serve the deterministic paths and the local guaranteed reply as a 200 stream. Keep fail-closed only for the paid model call.

rows.requirement: Timeouts per stage, plus a client budget (no infinite 'thinking')
rows.gap: A hung provider or DB call keeps the user on 'يفكّر…' indefinitely, and auto-retry never fires because no error is raised.
rows.correction: Client: signal = AbortSignal.any([init.signal, controller.signal]), with a budget larger than the server deadline. Server: one turn deadline, AbortSignal.any([request.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(T)]), passed to generateText and the RAG stage, with supabase abortSignal on the pre-model RPCs. The RAG stage raced like the snapshot.

On the server, generateText gets only request.signal (chat.ts:806). getUser (331), org_members (345), rate (380), quota (390), the HCIS read (574-579) and prefs (725) have no deadline. Bounded stages: snapshot at 2.5s (sadeed-context.server.ts:20,127-135) and embeddings (gemini-embeddings.server.ts:107-108, timeoutMs 15000, retries 2).

rows.requirement: Context window / history management
rows.gap: Nothing blocking. The client sends 20 messages and the server keeps 12, so up to 8 messages are uploaded and dropped. There is no summary of dropped turns.
rows.correction: Optional: align the client window to the server's 12 merged turns, or add a rolling summary.

rows.requirement: Memory persistence and recall (finn_memory / aria_conversations) feeding later turns
rows.gap: Cross-turn memory works only if the flag is on and the memory RPC works, and neither is confirmed. The Article 26 capture job's sources (aria_conversations / aria_learning_log) receive nothing from chat.
rows.correction: Fix the aria_match_* bodies to finn_* in a reviewed migration (data-engineer), or move to a single retrieval RPC. Write chat turns to the table the capture job reads, or point the job at finn_interactions. Use waitUntil for the writes (CHAT-15).

rows.requirement: Conversation continuity across reloads (threads/messages)
rows.gap: Reloading the page loses the whole conversation. Thread history is never written or loaded.
rows.correction: For authenticated users, create or reuse a threads row (UUID) and send it as threadId. On mount, load the last N messages from messages. Guests: sessionStorage. Then the existing persistence block becomes live.

rows.requirement: Pre-model context retrieval (RAG) grounded, org-scoped and observable
rows.gap: Chat answers get no document grounding. Regulatory questions fall to the gateway's 'غير متوفر' unless the HCIS reference rows load (finalize.ts evidence rule). There are two divergent retrieval systems in one turn: 768-d aria_match_* before the model, and 1536-d hybrid via the tool.
rows.correction: Pick one path (owner/architect). Either fix the aria_match_* SQL bodies to finn_* with an org filter, or route pre-model retrieval through retrieveWithEvidenceGate with orgId. Add a stage deadline and a rag_query_log row per attempt. Remove the dead branch, or inject RAG regardless of liveDataAvailable.

Overstated sub-point: the dead branch chat.ts:544-552 rarely matters, because buildSadeedContextSnapshot returns hasOperationalData:true on DB timeout, empty or error via buildProductionDatasetsSnapshot (sadeed-context.server.ts:131-134, 384-388). rows.requirement: Post-response work lifecycle on Workers (persistence/telemetry must complete or be explicitly best-effort)
rows.gap: Workers do not guarantee unawaited promises once the response is done, so telemetry and memory rows may be silently lost. The actual loss rate is not measured.
rows.correction: Expose the Workers ExecutionContext to the handler and wrap the persistence in ctx.waitUntil(...). Alternatively, await the persistence inside the stream's execute() after text-end.

rows.requirement: Untrusted retrieved/live context sanitization before the prompt and in the output gateway
rows.gap: A poisoned KB or document chunk reaches the model with its override phrasing intact, and the gateway's injection check has no input.
rows.correction: Pass every retrieved excerpt through safeExcerpt / sanitizeRetrievedContent before it enters the prompt. Pass retrievedDocs (the excerpts) to finalizeSadeedOutput.

rows.requirement: Output gateway reports executed tool actions truthfully
rows.gap: The user is told an action awaits approval when it already ran, which invites a repeat (duplicate email, SMS or permit decision; see CHAT-05).
rows.correction: Build trusted receipts from successful tool results of the same request (tool name, ok, ref/id) and pass them as executionReceipt/action to finalize. Alternatively, have the gateway exempt claims backed by a same-turn ok tool result.

'تم الإرسال إلى المالك بنجاح عبر البريد.' and 'تم الاعتماد للتصريح PTW-1001…' both became approval_required/unbacked-execution-claim (finalize.ts:411-416, RE_EXEC_CLAIM 160-161). 'تم تسجيل البلاغ…' passed as answer. chat.ts:839-848 passes no action or executionReceipt and never reads gen.steps. The tools do execute: the direct owner send at sadeed-tools.server.ts:337-347, and the sec_decide_permit update at ~897 for platform admins.

rows.requirement: TTFT and per-stage latency telemetry
rows.gap: The owner's main complaint (speed) cannot be measured, and control ④ of the 2026-10-11 answer-path exception (before/after measurement in the commit) cannot be met with real data.
rows.correction: Record t0 at handler entry. Measure each stage (body, auth, org, rate, quota, ctx, rag, prefs, model, finalize). Emit a Server-Timing header and a structured log line. Write the real total to finn_interactions.latency_ms. Once streaming exists, set firstTokenAt on the first delta. Add a workflow_dispatch benchmark against the preview.

This is observability, not correctness: a before/after TTFB can still be taken with a scripted preview fetch, so P2.

rows.requirement: Caching (prompt prefix / provider context cache / response cache)
rows.gap: Every turn pays full prefill for about 45k chars or more (guest), and more for authenticated turns with 31 tool definitions (14.6k chars measured). Any implicit provider prefix caching is defeated by design.
rows.correction: Keep the static SYSTEM_PROMPT plus tools as a byte-stable prefix and append the runtime clock block at the end (or as the final system section). Consider a Gemini explicit cache for the static part. This needs an owner ruling on the 'at the very start' placement (see conflicts).

rows.requirement: Simple-request fast path (Article 22 §3: deterministic answer before the model, under 400ms)
rows.gap: The '<400ms' promise depends on 3-5 DB/Auth round trips that have no timeout (CHAT-10).
rows.correction: Run the text-only matchers right after validation, behind one combined rate-limit RPC, before the auth/org lookups. Do not charge the AI quota for no-model replies.

rows.requirement: Critical-path parallelism before the model call
rows.gap: Avoidable round trips: rate limit and 2 quota checks could be one RPC or parallel. getUser plus org_members could be a local JWT verify plus one query. Preferences and HCIS could join the snapshot Promise.all.
rows.correction: Merge rate and quota into one RPC (or Promise.all). Use auth.getClaims (local JWKS) and run the org lookup in parallel with rate/quota. Move loadAdaptivePreferenceBlock and the HCIS read into the existing Promise.all.
rows.verifier: **Verified** (adversarial pass): Sequence confirmed: getUser 331 → org_members 345 → check_rate_limit 380 → quota global then identity (ai-quota.server.ts:182-224, sequential) → Promise.all snapshot‖RAG 493 → conditional HCIS 574 → prefs 725 → generateText 795. Guests make 3 network calls. Constitution Art 28(e) concerns route SSR server-fn fan-out, not this handler, so the citation is misapplied. This is a latency improvement, P2.

rows.requirement: Guest path and rate limiting (per-visitor fairness)
rows.gap: If the env var is unset, a few concurrent demo visitors exhaust a single global guest bucket within minutes.

Only chat.ts and sadeed-transcribe.ts:15 read the variable; no config or doc in the repo sets it. Guests get 12 requests per 300s (chat.ts:381) plus a 120/day identity quota (ai-quota.server.ts:113-115), all on 'ip:shared'. The production value of the env var is not measured.

rows.requirement: Reply-mode contract matches the channel (typed text vs spoken)
rows.gap: Typed executive reports get compressed into spoken prose by default.
rows.correction: Owner decision. Recommended: separate 'speak it' from the 'voice contract'. Typed turns send replyMode 'text', and speech is derived client-side with toSadeedSpeechText (which already exists). The voice contract applies only to mic turns.

rows.requirement: Model call configuration proportional to the request (tools/steps per intent)
rows.gap: Large fixed prompt overhead and up to 12 sequential model round trips before any byte reaches the user.
rows.correction: Subset tools by intent (read-only set for informational questions), lower the default step cap, set per-step timeouts, and route copilot submits through sadeedBrain so the hint is current.

rows.requirement: Voice conversation never dies (layer 3)
rows.gap: None for continuity. Retry classification issues are covered in CHAT-04.
rows.correction: None.

rows.requirement: Request validation and payload limits at the chat API
rows.gap: English error texts are covered in CHAT-07. Magic-byte inspection of attachments is not wired: src/lib/security/file-inspection.server.ts is imported only by its own test.
rows.correction: Optional: run inspectSadeedAttachment on the last-message file parts.

rows.requirement: Explicit deep (Council) review reachable when requested
rows.gap: The council is unreachable from the UI. The capability is kept but dormant.
rows.correction: Owner decision: add an explicit 'مراجعة معمّقة' action that sets replyMode 'deep', or document it as API-only.

rows.requirement: Capability readiness = OR across capable keys (/api/chat/health)
rows.gap: ok is always true and provider reachability is not probed, which is acceptable for a key-presence probe. rag_ready is the simplest way to confirm SADEED_GEMINI_RAG_READY in production (not done from this sandbox: prod domains are blocked).
rows.correction: None. The lead can read rag_ready from production health to settle CHAT-12/CHAT-14.

rows.requirement: PDF (text layer) is extracted with structure, chunked, embedded and usable later
rows.gap: Line breaks (hasEOL) and page boundaries are lost. RTL item order is not handled (not measured). A PDF attached in chat never reaches the knowledge base. No server-side extraction.
rows.correction: Extract per page ({page,text}) and honor hasEOL. Carry the page into chunk metadata. Route chat PDFs through the same extractor and deposit them.

rows.requirement: Scanned/image-only PDF gets OCR during ingestion
rows.gap: Scanned SOPs cannot be ingested at all.
rows.correction: Add a server-side OCR fallback (Gemini file-to-text) when the text layer is empty, marked metadata.ocr=true.

rows.requirement: DOCX is extracted with headings and tables and accepted in every entry point
rows.gap: Structure is lost on the knowledge page, and DOCX is rejected in chat.
rows.correction: Use mammoth convertToHtml and convert to markdown so tables and headings survive. Accept DOCX in chat through server extraction and deposit it.

rows.requirement: Legacy .doc is handled explicitly
rows.gap: No conversion and no tailored Arabic guidance.
rows.correction: Show the Arabic message 'حوّل الملف إلى DOCX' or convert on the server.

rows.requirement: TXT is ingested faithfully, including the encoding
rows.gap: Windows-1256 Arabic text becomes U+FFFD mojibake with no detection. There is no end-to-end test.
rows.correction: Detect the encoding: retry with TextDecoder('windows-1256') when the replacement-character ratio is high.

rows.requirement: RTF is supported or rejected cleanly
rows.gap: Depending on the browser, RTF is either rejected or ingested as raw markup.
rows.correction: Reject RTF explicitly, or strip RTF on the server.

rows.requirement: Markdown ingested with structure
rows.gap: Chunking ignores headings.
rows.correction: Split chunks on headings and keep the heading path in metadata.

rows.requirement: HTML converted to text or rejected
rows.gap: Tags and scripts become knowledge chunks. The accept list and extractText disagree.
rows.correction: Strip HTML to text, or reject it. Align the accept attribute with extractText.

rows.requirement: CSV ingested in a table-aware way
rows.gap: Header context is lost per chunk. Arabic Excel CSVs (cp1256) are garbled.
rows.correction: Use row-group chunks that repeat the header row, plus an encoding fallback.

rows.requirement: XLSX/XLS supported in the canonical path
rows.gap: Spreadsheets reach knowledge only through the legacy path, which has its own defects (INGEST-17 and INGEST-30).
rows.correction: Move sheet extraction into the canonical path (enqueueKnowledgeIngest/hook).

rows.requirement: JSON ingested meaningfully
rows.gap: No flattening by key path. Model acceptance is unverified.
rows.correction: Flatten into key-path lines before chunking. Verify Gemini MIME support or send the content as text.

rows.requirement: XML handled
rows.gap: Raw markup goes into chunks, and the paths behave differently.
rows.correction: Strip tags to text, or reject.

rows.requirement: PPTX supported
rows.gap: Training and SOP decks cannot be ingested.
rows.correction: Extract slide text and notes on the server, recording the slide number as the page.

rows.requirement: Images (PNG/JPG/WEBP) are read, and OCR text is indexed
rows.gap: There is no OCR-to-knowledge, and image content is lost after one turn.
rows.correction: Optionally OCR an attached image on the server into a deposited document.

rows.requirement: Audio files can be transcribed into knowledge
rows.gap: Recorded briefings cannot become knowledge.
rows.correction: Add an audio upload that transcribes, then ingests the transcript (if the owner wants it).

rows.requirement: Source-code files handled by an explicit policy
rows.gap: The two paths behave differently, and no policy is stated.
rows.correction: Decide on a policy (owner) and enforce one allowlist across both paths.

rows.requirement: One canonical ingestion pipeline (one chunker, limit, readiness rule)
rows.gap: Limits, chunking, readiness and dedupe diverge by entry point.
rows.correction: Retire ingestSadeedDocument and point /sadeed-documents uploads at enqueueKnowledgeIngest. Archive rag-ingest per the 2026/10/11 decision to build on the finn_* tables.

rows.requirement: Real file-signature (magic-byte) validation before storage, extraction or model
rows.gap: Any bytes labelled application/pdf reach Gemini or storage.
rows.correction: Run inspectSadeedAttachment on the server: in /api/chat for file parts, and on the stored object before ingest. Set allowed_mime_types on the buckets.

rows.requirement: Size limits enforced consistently at every layer
rows.gap: No byte cap exists on knowledge uploads or in storage, and the advertised limit is false.
rows.correction: Cap bytes on the client, set the bucket file_size_limit, and stream-limit the chat body.

rows.requirement: Originals stored reliably, linked to their document, retrievable and never orphaned
rows.gap: Originals can be silently missing, are never downloadable, and can be orphaned.
rows.correction: Surface storage failures, slice the title to 300 characters, add a source-download action, and add a bucket lifecycle sweep for objects with no row.

rows.requirement: Large documents are processed asynchronously
rows.gap: The 'enqueue' naming is misleading: everything runs synchronously. Wall-clock time and platform timeout behaviour were not measured.
rows.correction: Persist a job and return immediately. Process in a background task (waitUntil or a queue) with a server-side status.

rows.requirement: The privileged hook secret is never sent to an origin derived from request input
rows.gap: If Host can be spoofed, an authenticated user can exfiltrate CRON_HOOK_SECRET. The call is also a Worker subrequest to itself.
rows.correction: Call the ingest core in-process as a shared function instead of over HTTP, or pin the base URL from env.

Exploitability is not measured. The default Lovable target is Cloudflare (vite.config.ts:16-17), where a Worker receives only hostnames routed to it, so an attacker-chosen origin is platform-constrained; the expected risk is lower than P1.

rows.requirement: Truthful, granular progress
rows.gap: No per-chunk progress, and the stats payload is heavy.
rows.correction: Store processed/total chunks on the row, and count with 'embedding is not null' in SQL.

rows.requirement: Idempotent, atomic de-duplication
rows.gap: Concurrent duplicates and re-extraction variance both slip through.
rows.correction: Add a partial unique index on (org_id, user_id, revision_hash) WHERE status in ('pending','processing','ready'), and collapse internal whitespace in the hash normalization.

rows.requirement: The chunk upsert has a matching unique constraint in production
rows.gap: If the index is not unique, every knowledge-upload and chat-deposit ingest ends 'failed'. Which path produced the 8 'ready' prod documents was not measured.
rows.correction: If the index is not unique, add a UNIQUE index on (document_id, chunk_index) after checking for duplicates.

The only UNIQUE(document_id,chunk_index) is in the unapplied 20260728093300_rag_chunks.sql:64, which targets a different table. The lead's prod listing marks UNIQUE only on finn_documents. Not measured; the suggested pg_indexes and model_version queries would settle it.

rows.requirement: Retries and recovery for failed or stuck ingests
rows.gap: Rows get stuck pending or processing, and failed rows pile up.
rows.correction: Mark the row failed before throwing. Add a retry action and a cron sweeper that fails stale rows.

rows.requirement: Page numbers preserved for citations
rows.gap: Citations cannot point to a page or section.
rows.correction: Record per-page offsets during extraction, map each chunk to a page range, and include it in the citation tag.

rows.requirement: Document versioning and replacement
rows.gap: Old and revised SOPs coexist, and both are 'ready'.
rows.correction: Add replace(document_id) that re-ingests in place, or a superseded_by/is_current flag that retrieval filters on.

rows.requirement: Deletion removes row, chunks and storage object, after confirmation
rows.gap: A failed row delete leaves a row pointing at a deleted file. There is no human confirmation gate.
rows.correction: Delete the row first (returning storage_path), then the object, checking both errors. Add a confirm dialog.

rows.requirement: Status 'ready' only after complete, verified indexing
rows.gap: The legacy path reports 'ready' with missing vectors and truncated text. 'Ready' is never proven retrievable.
rows.correction: Fold the legacy path into the hook (INGEST-17). Define 'ready' as all chunks embedded plus a self-retrieval probe that finds the document's own chunk.
rows.verifier: **Verified** (adversarial pass): Confirmed on the live legacy path (sadeed-documents.tsx:93 → ingestSadeedDocument). documents.functions.ts:146 stores a null embedding when embed fails. 160-167 sets 'ready' unconditionally. 49 silently caps at slice(0,400) chunks, while the input allows 2,000,000 chars (91). citation_ready only checks that chunks are embedded (knowledge-upload.functions.ts:194).

rows.requirement: Lossless, structure-aware chunking
rows.gap: It has no awareness of headings, pages or tables. The overlap is a raw character tail and can split words. The only contextual header is the title, inside the embedding prompt.
rows.correction: Split on structure boundaries, overlap on word boundaries, and prepend a short section header to each chunk.

rows.requirement: Efficient embedding with cost and abuse controls
rows.gap: Paid embedding runs per user are unbounded (dedupe blocks only identical text).
rows.correction: Use embedGeminiBatch, and add a per-user ingest rate limit plus an AI quota.

rows.requirement: Indexing makes chunks retrievable (ANN sized to corpus, lexical index)
rows.gap: An 'indexed' chunk can be missed by ANN search, and there is no lexical fallback.

Latency MODEL (from code, not measured). Guest model turn: T_first_byte ≈ upload + 3×RTT_db (rate, quota-global, quota-id) + [cold isolate: dataset module load/parse] + T_gemini(full buffered generation: prefill of a system prompt of about 51-61k chars, then all output tokens; 700-token cap when replyMode=voice, the default) + finalize (sync, CPU). Authenticated turn: upload + RTT_auth(getUser) + RTT_db(org_members) + 3×RTT_db + max(snapshot ≤2.5s, RAG[flag on]: RTT_gemini_embed (≤3×15s) + RTT_rpc + RTT_db_update) + [HCIS: RTT_db] + RTT_db(prefs) + Σ_steps(T_gemini_step + tool DB RTTs) (≤12 steps). Fast path: guest 3 RTTs, authenticated 5 RTTs, plus a match under 1ms. Voice time to first audio = T_first_byte + first-sentence TTS. Because the response is buffered, time to first byte equals total turn time on every model path.

Network vs local stages: network = Supabase Auth getUser; PostgREST org_members; 3 RPCs (check_rate_limit); 15 snapshot queries (parallel); Gemini embed; 3 aria_match RPCs; finn_memory update; finn_knowledge HCIS read; finn_adaptive_preferences read; Gemini generate (×steps); tool DB calls. Local = JSON validation, sanitizeHistory, scope/fast-recall/instant matchers, production datasets block, convertToModelMessages, finalize/seal.

The 'safe output gateway' (finalize.ts) is regex-based over the full model text (exec-claim, secret leak, exfiltration, KPI/time/evidence rules). This is the root reason streaming was removed. Per-token streaming is incompatible with it as written; per-sentence streaming would need a retract/replace path for whole-text rules.

The output gateway is not connected to tool execution: chat.ts never reads gen.steps/toolResults and passes no receipts. Executed writes can therefore be relabelled 'requires approval' (measured on 2 of 3 phrasings), and write tools run without any confirmation gate inside the turn.

The chat path holds two divergent retrieval systems: pre-model vector RAG (768-d, aria_match_*, user-only filter, broken in production with 42P01 per lead, swallowed errors, no rag_query_log) and the search_knowledge tool via retrieveWithEvidenceGate (hybrid sec_kb_hybrid_search, evidence gate, rag_query_log). The code constitution Art 31 mandates only the latter.

Persistence designed for continuity is disconnected: the singleton chat id 'sadeed-singleton' fails the UUID check, so threads/messages are never written; /assistant/$threadId ignores its param; no client storage. Memory (finn_memory) depends on SADEED_GEMINI_RAG_READY plus a likely-broken RPC. aria_conversations/aria_learning_log have no writer.

Resilience layers vs code: layer 1 (no-key local reply) exists; layer 2 client retry exists but is misclassified, and the server cooldown/alternate provider does not exist (Gemini-only policy); layer 3 voice continuity exists. A DB/RPC outage still yields a 503 through fail-closed rate limit/quota, even for no-model answers.

Client 30s timeout is ineffective for chat because AI SDK v6 always supplies init.signal (index.mjs:14208/14619) and sadeedAuthedFetch prefers it (sadeed-service.ts:46,59). Combined with the unbounded generateText and DB calls, a hang has no upper bound.

INGEST: Trace (canonical): /knowledge-upload extracts text in the browser (pdf.js, mammoth, File.text), uploads the original straight to the private aria-documents bucket (best effort, errors ignored), then calls enqueueKnowledgeIngest (requireSupabaseAuth). That inserts a finn_documents row (status 'pending'), runs a non-atomic dedupe, and makes a synchronous HTTP self-call with x-cron-secret to /api/public/hooks/sadeed-docs-ingest. The hook (service role) runs chunkText (1600/200), then Gemini embedContent per chunk (768 dims, concurrency 4), upserts finn_document_chunks, and marks the document 'ready'. Only extracted text crosses to the server; the server never reads the stored bytes.

Search is the dead end: the only chunk-level consumer is aria_match_documents. It is reached by chat (gatherRagContext, gated by SADEED_GEMINI_RAG_READY) and by /sadeed-documents search, and it fails in prod with 42P01. So all ingestion currently produces zero retrievable knowledge. The working hybrid search (sec_kb_hybrid_search) reads sec_knowledge_articles, which has no file-upload path; it is fed only by seeding plus kbEmbedMissing.

Three live writers plus one dead one write divergent corpora. (1) The hook path: 250k cap, no-loss chunker, dedupe. (2) The legacy ingestSadeedDocument behind /sadeed-documents (still linked from marketplace and enterprise search): 2M cap, 900/120 chunker that silently truncates past 400 chunks, null embeddings allowed with status 'ready', no revision_hash, chunk org_id left to the default org. (3) Chat depositTextFiles, which reuses (1) for text types only. (4) Dead: supabase/functions/rag-ingest targets rag_documents/rag_chunks at 1536 dims, with no caller and tables absent in prod.

Chat attachments are model-only and ephemeral. Allowlisted PDF, image, text, CSV, MD and JSON files go as inline base64 data URLs to Gemini for the current turn. Later turns see only '[Attachment metadata]'. Only text types are deposited, and only after the reply completes. No signature validation: the existing src/lib/security/file-inspection.server.ts is unused, and the aria-attachments-quarantine bucket and aria_attachment_scans table have no code references.

The answer-path gateway collides with attachments (measured). finalizeSadeedOutput's regulatory gate never counts attachments as evidence, so summaries of attached SEC documents are refused. Its RE_PHONE PII redaction rewrites ISO dates, decimal series and reference numbers to '[هاتف محجوب]'. The pre-model instant-data short-circuit ignores file parts.

Status semantics overclaim. 'Citation Ready' is defined as 'all chunks embedded' (getKnowledgeChunkStats) and the page prints 'SADEED can now cite this document', yet no retrieval check exists. 'Async/enqueue' is a synchronous request chain: for a 250k-char document that is 179–249 sequential-at-width-4 embedding calls, with no job record, sweeper or document-level retry.

Limits are unified only for extracted text (250,000 chars, enforced at four layers). Byte limits are absent on the knowledge page, the advertised 50MB is unenforced, and prod buckets have file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types NULL. Chat client and server caps differ (8/16MB versus 10/20MiB), and the 24MB body cap relies on the Content-Length header.

The hook invocation sends CRON_HOOK_SECRET to an origin derived from the incoming request URL instead of a pinned base URL or an in-process call. Exploitability depends on the platform's Host handling, which was not measured.

Production schema for the chunk upsert target is unknown. The hook's ON CONFLICT (document_id, chunk_index) needs a unique index that no migration creates. If prod's index is non-unique, every hook ingest fails with 42P10. The 8 'ready' prod documents could have come from the legacy path; model_version distribution would show which.
RAG: Three retrieval stacks coexist and do not share a contract. (1) Automatic chat RAG: gatherRagContext uses 768-dim legacy embeddings and the aria_match_* RPCs over the finn_* tables. It is vector-only, fails closed on flag/org, and RPC errors only produce console.warn (src/lib/sadeed/rag.server.ts:82-213). (2) Governed path: retrieveWithEvidenceGate embeds at 1536 dims and calls sec_kb_hybrid_search (RRF over dense, FTS and trigram) over sec_knowledge_articles, with an evidence gate. It is reached only from the search_knowledge chat tool and the rag.search_verified agent tool (src/lib/sadeed/rag/retrieve.server.ts). (3) Legacy sec_kb_search uses 768-dim kb-embed (kbSemanticSearch, agent kb.search). A fourth, unapplied stack (rag-retrieve edge function → rag_hybrid_search, 20260728*) sits behind a VITE flag. The runtime constitution (src/lib/sadeed/constitution.ts item 31) says ALL retrieval must go through retrieveWithEvidenceGate at 1536 dims. Stacks 1 and 3 violate that.

The ingestion pipeline shipped today (knowledge-ingest-core, sadeed-docs-ingest hook, knowledge-upload page) writes finn_documents/finn_document_chunks at vector(768). The only retrieval reader of those chunks is aria_match_documents, which fails in prod with 42P01. Ingestion therefore feeds a dead end: 8 documents and 18 chunks that no answer can ever use.

chat.ts has a control-flow bug: the guest/no-live-data branch sets liveDataAvailable=true (chat.ts:532), which makes the 'UNTRUSTED TENANT KNOWLEDGE' injection (chat.ts:544-552) unreachable. RAG text reaches the model only when the authenticated caller also has operational data. Its citations are still handed to the output gateway as available evidence (chat.ts:843).

Citation enforcement lives in the output gateway (finalize.ts:440-460). It is regex-triggered (regulatory claims only), it lets invented tags through whenever one real tag is present (measured), it refuses correct bare 'SEC-xx' citations (measured), and it ignores tool-sourced citations because evidence.available = ragCitations only. No UI renders citations (SadeedCopilot.tsx reads only metadata.envelope, for speech).

Injection defense is layered but uneven. Untrusted blocks are delimited, <> is escaped and an instruction hierarchy is stated (chat.ts:109-113, 516-551). sanitizeRetrievedContent and safeExcerpt are applied only to tool outputs. The auto-RAG contextBlock and uploaded content are not sanitized, and finalize's retrievedDocs injection check is never fed by chat.ts.

The gap-capture path is both broken and non-constitutional. search_knowledge calls rag_record_gap_for_org with `.rpc(...).catch(...)`. supabase-js builders have no .catch (measured: TypeError), so every non-passed gate outcome turns into a tool exception. The target table rag_gaps is absent in prod. The call sits inside a user request path, which Article 26 forbids.

Isolation in retrieval relies on RLS rather than explicit predicates. gatherRagContext gates on orgId but never passes it. aria_match_documents filters by user only (repo body). aria_match_knowledge is unfiltered. sec_kb_search has no org parameter. sec_kb_hybrid_search treats a NULL org as 'all orgs', and in prod anon has EXECUTE on it.

Observability is absent: rag_query_log has 0 rows in prod. The auto-RAG path never logs, early returns skip logging, and insert {error} results are ignored. firstTokenAt is a const null (chat.ts:718), so no TTFT is recorded either.

The measurement and gate machinery (src/lib/rag/evaluation.ts, tuning.ts, supabase/preflight/rag_measure.sql) is sound on Article 27 semantics (null rather than 0) but measures an unapplied schema (rag_hybrid_search). No runner targets the production RPCs, so recall and citation precision for production are 'not measured'.

SEC: Two parallel retrieval stacks. /api/chat uses gatherRagContext (rag.server.ts: 768-dim, aria_match_* RPCs, vector-only, no evidence gate, no rag_query_log, no PII sanitize). Tools and the orchestrator use retrieveWithEvidenceGate (rag/retrieve.server.ts: 1536-dim, sec_kb_hybrid_search RRF, injection screen, logging). The constitution (Art. 31) names only the second. In prod both are inert: the first because the aria_match_* bodies point at renamed tables (42P01), the second because SADEED_GEMINI_RAG_READY gates it and rag_query_log has 0 rows.

RAG failure is silent by design. gatherRagContext turns RPC errors into console.warn plus empty context (rag.server.ts:108-110), so the prod 42P01 never reaches the user, telemetry or rag_query_log. Breakage is undetectable without log scraping.

Guest chat context is built from git-bundled 'real' export JSON (maintenance-report.data.json, projects, event report) instead of the masked DB view. Whatever privacy masking the DB applies (maint_orders_v) does not cover this path, and that is the root cause of SEC-01.

Tenant scoping in /api/chat is derived server-side: org comes from org_members matched with app_metadata.current_org, and RAG fails closed on ambiguity. The service-role orchestrator path (agents.ts:418) shifts isolation from RLS to the SQL body's _org_id predicate.

Privileged ingest runs through an HTTP self-call carrying CRON_HOOK_SECRET to an origin derived from the request (knowledge-upload.functions.ts:118). The ingest core is already pure (knowledge-ingest-core.ts), so an in-process call would remove both the secret hop and the missing-timeout risk.

Rate limiting is DB-backed (check_rate_limit through supabaseAdmin) and fails closed (503). The chat guest identity collapses to one global 'shared' key unless TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true, and when enabled it prefers spoofable XFF over cf-connecting-ip, the reverse of the order used by sadeed-incident.ts and the public routes.

Security helpers exist but are unwired: src/lib/security/file-inspection.server.ts (zip-ratio/Office structure inspection) is imported only by its test, and rateLimitRag (rag/sanitize.server.ts:70) has no callers.

Storage defense is entirely policy-based. Prod buckets have no size or MIME limits, and the knowledge-upload client uploads the raw file with no size cap before server validation of the extracted text.
QA: The /api/chat model path is fully buffered. generateText (chat.ts:795) runs to completion with stopWhen stepCountIs(12) and maxRetries 2. The output then passes the finalizeSadeedOutput gateway and goes out as one text-delta (chat.ts:965-970). All fixed paths (local guaranteed reply chat.ts:285, scope-guard, fast-recall and instant-data chat.ts:422) are also single deltas. So the user's TTFT equals total server time; this is a deliberate 'Option A' (chat.ts:765-768).

The pre-model chain for an authenticated, grounded, text-mode turn has 11 awaits on every turn, plus 2 conditional ones: validateChatRequest/request.json (295), auth.getUser (331), org_members (345), enforceRateLimit RPC (380), enforceAiQuota with 2 sequential check_rate_limit RPCs (390; ai-quota.server.ts:182,204), instant-data import (462), module imports (489), Promise.all[snapshot raced vs deadline, rag: embed then 3 aria_match_* RPCs] (493), conditional HCIS finn_knowledge read (574), conditional deep council runAgentMission with a 50 s timeout (650), tools import (695), loadAdaptivePreferenceBlock (725), convertToModelMessages (798). That is 7 strictly sequential network round-trips (8 with RAG on, 9 with HCIS). A guest turn has 3 (rate plus 2 quota) before the production snapshot.

Telemetry undercounts. startAt is set at chat.ts:717, after every pre-model stage, so finn_interactions.latency_ms (chat.ts:889) and the 'buffered finish' log omit auth, rate, quota, snapshot and RAG time. first_token_ms is always null (const at :718). finn_interactions has no request_id. Guest turns write no interaction or incident rows (the `if (userId)` gate at :821 and :861).

Retrieval observability is disconnected. rag_query_log is written only by retrieveWithEvidenceGate.finish (retrieve.server.ts:136-157), on the search_knowledge tool and agent paths. The default chat retrieval, gatherRagContext (rag.server.ts:82-110), uses a different stack (768-dim embeddings.server.ts:9, aria_match_* RPCs, no injection screen, no sanitizeRetrievedContent, no rateLimitRag, no log). That contradicts the constitution's Article 31 as stated in src/lib/sadeed/constitution.ts:46 (1536 dims, every retrieval through retrieveWithEvidenceGate, every attempt logged).

The RAG embedding call does have a deadline: httpJson with timeoutMs 15_000 and retries 2 (gemini-embeddings.server.ts:98-108). It is not bound to request.signal, and the total worst case including retries was not measured.

Measured local cost notes. chunkText is negligible (≤3.9 ms max even at 250k characters), but the 200-character overlap inflates embedding input by about 1.18–1.21× (sumChunkChars/chars). A 250k-character document yields 226–241 chunks, below MAX_CHUNKS_PER_DOCUMENT=400, so 250k is not cap-bound. buildChatPdf scales about linearly: about 31 ms for 2 messages, 139 ms for 20, 536 ms for 80 (p50, Node on 4 vCPU). It runs client-side via downloadChatPdf, so on mobile main threads it is probably slower, but that was not measured.

Not measurable from this session, per Article 27: production TTFT, end-to-end chat latency, retrieval latency, indexing (embedding) time, throughput, and production error or timeout rates. The reasons: there is no production network (sandbox policy), no provider keys, rag_query_log has 0 rows, first_token_ms is always null, and latency_ms excludes the pre-model stages.

dimensions.dimension: 3. Context management & conversation continuity (context windows, memory)
dimensions.chatgpt: Per-plan ChatGPT context windows could not be confirmed from an official page; the pricing and help pages were unreachable. Third-party sources disagree. Instant model: Free 8K, 16K or 27K; Plus 32K or 54K; Pro/Enterprise 128K. Thinking: about 256K on paid plans and 400K on Pro. Memory (Memory FAQ) has two controls. 'Saved memories' are details the user explicitly asks it to keep; 'reference chat history' draws on past chats. A newer automatic memory system can be switched back to legacy saved memories. Temporary Chats neither use nor create memories. Deleting a chat does not delete memories saved from it.
dimensions.gemini: Google's Gemini Apps limits table, as reported in Sept 2025 coverage, lists 32K tokens with no AI plan and 1M tokens on Google AI Pro and Ultra. Deep Think on Ultra is capped at 192K. The 128K figure for AI Plus is third-party only and unconfirmed. Notebooks in Gemini (Google blog, April 2026) are personal knowledge bases. They hold moved chats, custom instructions and files, and sync with NotebookLM. At launch they were for AI Plus/Pro/Ultra on web only. A per-notebook memory option is reported by third parties only. The official 'past chats/personal context' help page was not retrieved.
dimensions.claude: API: Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5/5.1 and Mythos 5/5.1/Preview have a 1M-token context window by default, with no beta header. These models allow up to 128K output tokens. Other models, including Sonnet 4.5 (deprecated), have 200K. Server-side compaction is in beta for 4.6+ models; context editing can clear old tool results and thinking blocks. claude.ai may manage context on a rolling FIFO basis. Apps: memory is stored by topic. It is on by default for Free, Pro and Max and off by default for Team and Enterprise, and each project has its own memory. Paid plans can search past chats (shown as RAG tool calls). Incognito chats are left out of history and memory.

dimensions.chatgpt: Projects hold files. Two versions of the File Uploads FAQ give different limits. Older: Plus 20 files per project; Pro, Team, Edu and Business 40. Newer: Free 5; Go and Plus 25; Edu, Pro, Business and Enterprise 40. API: the file search tool attaches file_citation annotations (file id, filename, index) to output text.
dimensions.gemini: App: Notebooks in Gemini sync sources both ways with NotebookLM (April 2026). API: Grounding with Google Search returns groundingMetadata for grounded answers. The Gemini API File Search tool was not covered in this pass.
dimensions.claude: Projects have a knowledge base. When project knowledge nears the context limit, Claude switches to RAG mode automatically. Anthropic says this expands capacity 'up to 10x', with no setup, on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. API: citations work on document and search_result blocks, so RAG chunks can be grounded and cited.

dimensions.dimension: 5. File uploads & multimodal inputs — formats and size/count limits
dimensions.chatgpt: The File Uploads FAQ was read only through search summaries, but its figures matched across every version found. 512MB hard limit per file. Text and document files are capped at 2M tokens each; this cap does not apply to spreadsheets. CSV and spreadsheets: about 50MB, depending on row size. Images: 20MB each. Caps: 25GB per end user and 100GB per organization. Up to 80 files every 3 hours, and Free users get 3 uploads per day. OpenAI says it may lower these limits at peak hours.
dimensions.gemini: Gemini app (help article 14903178): up to 10 files per prompt, with each file in a folder counting toward that. Videos up to 2GB; other supported files up to 100MB. Total video length of 5 minutes comes from a university mirror of Google's text and is unconfirmed on the official page. A Google AI plan raises the limits. Rolling quotas show a 'limit for chats with files' message. Gemini API: the Files API allows 2GB per file and 20GB per project, and files are deleted after 48 hours. PDFs up to 1,000 pages, at 258 tokens per page. Sources disagree on the inline request limit: 20MB, 50MB for PDFs, or 100MB.
dimensions.claude: Apps (article updated July 23, 2026). Documents: PDF, DOCX, CSV, TXT, HTML, ODT, RTF, EPUB, JSON and XLSX; XLSX needs code execution enabled. Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP. In chat: 500MB per file, up to 20 files per chat, images up to 8000x8000 px. PDFs up to 1,000 pages: 100 pages or fewer get text and visual analysis, 101–1,000 pages text only, and longer PDFs are rejected. Project files: 30MB each, with unlimited count as long as the total fits the context window (text only, except multimodal PDFs). Conflict: the 'Create and edit files' article gives 30MB per file for uploads and downloads. API: up to 600 images or PDF pages per request (100 on 200K-context models); request-size limits can be hit before token limits.

If input exceeds the window, the API returns 400 'prompt is too long'. On 4.5+ models, generation that hits the limit stops with stop_reason model_context_window_exceeded. Apps: PDFs up to 1,000 pages, with only the first 100 pages analysed visually. Project RAG expands capacity about 10x. The docs warn that recall degrades as context grows ('context rot').

dimensions.claude: Voice mode is in beta on every plan (Free, Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) on mobile, Desktop and web. It offers push-to-talk and a hands-free mode where speaking interrupts Claude. Text transcripts are saved to chat history, and voice counts toward usage limits. It is not available in Cowork or Claude Code, which offer dictation only. dimensions.chatgpt: From OpenAI's business-data page. Qualifying organizations set their own retention for business data, and the API Platform offers zero data retention. Data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, and Enterprise Key Management is available. Eligible ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare and API customers can keep content at rest in the US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India or the UAE. In-region GPU inference is available in the US or Europe. OpenAI says it does not train on business data by default: 'We do not train on your business data or conversations.' dimensions.gemini: Gemini in Workspace apps (Gmail, Docs, Drive and others) uses your content to answer prompts but not to train or improve Gemini or other generative models. It does not keep prompts or outputs without permission. Consumer Gemini on a personal account may use activity to improve services, including training, and a subset of chats is reviewed by humans. Workspace Labs falls under personal-account terms. Gemini data regions and client-side encryption were not verified in this pass.
dimensions.claude: Enterprise includes SSO, domain capture, SCIM (Entra syncs about every 40 minutes), role-based permissions, audit logs, the Compliance API (activity logs, chats, files) and an optional US-only inference. Custom retention can be set by the Primary Owner or Owner, with a 30-day minimum. Without it, data is kept indefinitely. It covers chats and projects but not Claude Design, Managed Agents, Cowork cloud sessions or scheduled tasks. Shortening retention schedules deletion immediately, and retention changes are written to audit logs. The public-sector FAQ says Enterprise data is not used for training. A separate 30-day retention rule applies to 'Covered Models', including for ZDR setups.
